summary: A specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies, Morrell studied at Stanford University until circa 1969 under Robert H. Brower, Edward Seidensticker, William H. McCullough, and Atsuyoshi Sakakura. He held a post at Washington University in St. Louis from circa 1968 to 1999.

Working in Indology and other fields, Svoboda studied at the University of Oklahoma (circa 1970–1972) and under mentor Vimalananda (circa 1978–1986). He served as an adjunct member at the Ayurvedic Institute, Bastyr University, and the Institute for Religion and Health.

Rhodes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who pursued doctoral studies at Harvard University. He became a professor at Otani University circa 1990 and served as a committee member for the Otani Society until 2000.
Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Florida served as Dean of Arts and Professor of Religion at Brandon University. He later held the post of Emeritus Fellow at the University of Victoria.

A scholar of Sinology and religious studies, Campany was a professor at Indiana University (circa 1989–2006). He later held posts at the University of Southern California (circa 2006–2010) and Vanderbilt University (circa 2010).

Gardner worked in Indology and other fields, studying at Harvard University from circa 1946 to 1958. He held posts at the University of Puget Sound and served as a professor at Harvard University in 1974.

A scholar of Japanology, Brower studied at Harvard University (circa 1940–1944) and the University of Michigan (circa 1949–1952). From circa 1966 to 1988, he served as Chairman of the Department of Far Eastern Languages and Literatures at Michigan.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology, Sharf earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez. He taught at McMaster University, the University of Michigan, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Miller served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1955 to 1989. He also held a professorship with the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Kritzer specializes in Buddhist studies, completing his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley (circa 1988–1995) under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He later served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University from circa 1999 to 2002.

Active in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Brown was a curator of South and Southeast Asian art at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (circa 1982–2014) and a professor at UCLA (circa 1987–2014).

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Lenz studied at Tartu Governorate Gymnasium and the Imperial University of Dorpat (1825–1828). From circa 1835 to 1836, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, Gimello completed his PhD at Columbia University (circa 1969–1976). He headed the Department of Oriental Studies at the University of Arizona (circa 1981–2006) and was a professor at Harvard (circa 2000–2006).

Maclagan worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Addiscombe Military Seminary (circa 1837–1839) and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Working in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, Magliola earned his PhD from Princeton University (circa 1966–1970). He held chair and professorial posts at National Taiwan University (circa 1989–1993) and Assumption University (circa 1993–2003).

Mayer is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Bristol and Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. In 2002, he joined the Oriental Studies faculty at Oxford University.

A philosopher educated at Princeton, Princeton Theological Seminary, Oxford, and Cornell, Adams held posts at the University of Michigan, UCLA (1972–1993), Yale University (1993–2004), the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (2009–2013), and Rutgers University (2013–2015).

A scholar of religious studies and Japanology, Bellah studied at Harvard College (circa 1946–1950) and Harvard University (circa 1950–1955). He held an academic post at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1967 to 1997.

Cust worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Eton College (circa 1834–1840) and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (circa 1840–1842). He held a post with the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.

An Indologist, Goldman studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania, and under T. S. Srinivasa Sastri and Shivaram Dattatray Joshi. He served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1971 to 2012.
